influences.name: Dave Fridmann

influences.name: Spacemen 3
influences.context: When we were at Toe Rag the bass amp was the best I've ever played through in my entire life, by far. It's the Selmer Treble 'N' Bass, like Spacemen 3 used

influences.name: Todd Rundgren
influences.context: I imagine you're a fan of Rundgren though, and that he doesn't do remixes like this often... Just the fact that he was going to be interacting with our music in some way was the big thing for me.

influences.name: Stephen Hawking
influences.context: As a kid, he poured through yellowed pages of Stephen Hawking books.

influences.name: Marilyn Manson
influences.context: I think it was Marilyn Manson that said, 'I don't make albums for my fans. I make them for a new audience.'

influences.name: Backstreet Boys
influences.context: Even though the sound is totally gnarled and blown out, to me it sounded like Backstreet Boys in some of it, or it sounded like Prince.

influences.name: Supertramp
influences.context: I didn't know if it sounded like Supertramp or The Chemical Brothers or Pharrell Williams. I could hear all those kind of things.

influences.name: MGMT
influences.context: For example, 'Electric Feel' by MGMT is in 6/4, so every bar that should have four beats has six beats.

influences.name: Air
influences.context: Getting into Air was the first time that I appreciated synthesizers as something that could be part of a craft, rather than synths being a sort of tool to get the most laser-beam-like present sound. I always just appreciated Air for having all these amazingly lush sounds.

influences.name: Daft Punk
influences.context: Someone sent me a Daft Punk song the other day. I was like "Oh, that's good." It just makes me want to go into the studio right now.

influences.name: Bee Gees
influences.context: The initial version of "The Less I Know the Better" had a distinct disco vibe, which Parker candidly compared to the Bee Gees.

influences.name: 1980s music
influences.context: By the time he was creating "Currents," Parker was gravitating towards the sounds of the 1980s, although he was initially hesitant to fully embrace this influence. "It was always music that I was into but just music that I'd kind of shied away from making because I figured like my world was weird expansive psych rock."
